review_notes: The whole file is one private helper, `eq_of_mem_zpowers_of_ne_one`, with a five-line proof. It contains no repeated blocks, so nothing here is repeated proof machinery. I grepped the repo for `zpow_mod_orderOf` and found the same reduction in other files. Examples are `CFSG/GH74/M12/HypGroup.lean` (`eq_one_or_eq_of_mem_zpowers_of_orderOf_two`), `CFSG/Walter/JRFacts.lean` (`eq_one_or_eq_of_mem_zpowers`) and an inline block in `CFSG/StandardComponent/AschbacherSeitz/A5Child.lean` (the `hinf` proof, around line 271). These are cross-file near-duplicates of a short parity case split on `k % 2`. Under the rubric that is a short calculation, and a shared lemma would only replace a few lines with a wrapper. It is also a duplicated-lemma consolidation question, not duplicated proof machinery in this file's proofs. I did not report a finding. I did not check whether Mathlib already has an equivalent order-2 zpowers lemma.
